verdict.rationale: Reader's own GitHub docs say images on a page that lack an alt tag can be auto-captioned by a vision-language model. The captions are inlined into the markdown output so a downstream text-only LLM can reason about them, which is exactly the story's goal. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the captions work well, documentation of the exact parameter that enables captioning, and clarity on images that already have alt text (only alt-less images are described as captioned).

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can get automatic captions for images on a page so a text-only model can reason about visual content

citations.quote: All images on a page that lack an `alt` tag can be auto-captioned by a VLM (vision-language model) and formatted as `![Image [idx]: [VLM_caption]](img_URL)`
Images — captioned by a vision-language model, so your downstream text-only LLM gets *just enough* hints to reason about them.
